items.summary: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02006-x A temporally super-resolved single-shot method overcomes the long-standing temporal–spectral trade-off in time-stretch spectroscopy. The outcome is continuous measurements of non-repetitive spectral dynamics with picosecond resolution, providing a three-orders-of-magnitude improvement over the current state of the art.

items.title: One super sensor from many

items.title: Optomechanics for piconewton force metrology
items.summary: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02011-0 Of the sensors that can directly sense forces in the pico- and sub-pico-newton ranges, only a few can measure in liquids. items.title: Microchip Nd:YAG laser with master-oscillator–power-amplifier architecture

A double-resonant microring seed with a 2.9 μW threshold is combined with waveguide amplifiers, enabling continuous-wave output powers exceeding 12 dBm.

items.title: Protons ride moving waves to reach record energy with long-pulse lasers
items.summary: Imagine a proton catching a wave and surfing it to gain speed. While the imagery may seem wild, the premise of laser-driven ion acceleration has promise as an alternative to conventional accelerators. However, the ultrathin targets used to drive this increase in ion energy are vulnerable to the weak prepulse that precedes the main high-intensity laser pulse, meaning an adaptation in the process is necessary.

items.title: A laser that stays locked without active control
items.summary: EPFL researchers have developed a chip-based laser that keeps a very stable frequency across its tested operating range, without needing active electronic control. Their research is published in the journal Nature Photonics.

items.title: Letting light wander through milk—a surprising approach to better imaging
items.summary: Light scattered in tissue usually ceases to be a useful source of information. But what if, instead of forcing it to travel along a single path, we allowed it to wander a little differently each time? Scientists from ICTER tested this seemingly risky idea and showed that a series of measurements that differ from one another can produce a clearer image than a single frame.

items.title: 3D light fields push electrons into quantum states previously beyond experimental reach
items.summary: By superimposing two ultrashort laser pulses that converge from different directions, a team of physicists at the University of Oldenburg has succeeded in generating three-dimensional light fields.

items.title: Physicists identify 'octupolar' magnetism, with implications for quantum technologies
items.summary: Most magnets have two poles: north and south, or positive and negative, in a familiar arrangement called a "dipole." But researchers are increasingly uncovering more complex forms of magnetism.

items.title: Laser-made muons produce first images of dense objects
items.summary: Muons are constantly being created as cosmic rays collide with molecules in Earth's upper atmosphere. With their ability to penetrate far into dense, solid materials, these cosmic muons are often used to image the insides of objects that are otherwise hidden from view. However, the flow of these natural particles is far too slow for the technique to become both fast and reliable in practical settings.

items.title: Rotating light pattern reveals laser frequency in a single image
items.summary: An international team of physicists has developed a new method for determining the precise color of laser light using an image that rotates as the laser's frequency shifts.

items.title: How to balance quantum batteries' high power with stable energy delivery
items.summary: Quantum batteries are an emerging area of research, with progress coming from theoretical studies and proof-of-principle experiments in small quantum systems. Unlike conventional chemical batteries used in everyday life, they use quantum systems to store and transfer energy. Researchers are exploring them as potential future energy sources for quantum processors and other quantum technologies.
